newsitem.title: PANAMA: Ousted Ecuadoran scoffs at corruption trial.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Ecuadoran scoffs at corruption trial.

text.p: Ousted Ecuadoran president Abdala Bucaram scoffed at moves by his country's new government to put him on trial for corruption on Friday.
"Everyone knows it's just political persecution," the controversial populist politician said while playing soccer.
"I'm not afraid of the trial. Now I'm enjoying myself with the Panamanian people," he said at a working-class district gymnasium where he plays soccer and basketball twice a week.
Bucaram moved to Panama City after Ecuador's Congress stripped him of the presidency a month ago citing "mental incompetence."
Ecuador's Supreme Court began criminal proceedings against the deposed president on Friday on charges of corruption and issued orders for the arrest of three of his aides.
Bucaram dismissed allegations that he misused $76 million during his six months in office and called on Latin American nations to help him return to office.
Bucaram lived in exile in Panama from 1985-90 after he fled Ecuador when he was charged with corruption as mayor of Guayaquil.
